segments.summary: Reviewed discovery, manifests, lifecycle, hook registry/signatures, mutation paths, return semantics, and custom-tool routing. Strong deterministic and central-policy baselines coexist with critical permission-override, fail-open, privileged-mutation, and lifecycle gaps.

Reviewed configuration, Persona/child inheritance, event logging, GUI, baseline deltas, acceptance criteria, blocked-hook addenda, owner map, and PLUG-002/003. Found an internal hook-name conflict and underspecified catalog and GUI edge behavior.

Reviewed terminology routing, central policy boundaries, definitions, discovery, manifest, and deduplication units. Core ordering is coherent; PLUG-006 lacks operational oracles and PLUG-009 preserves conflicting entry-format tokens.

Reviewed approval, load order, lifecycle, hook ordering, PluginContext, registry, and tool-hook grouping. Approval and API boundaries are strong; lifecycle failure semantics and registry consistency remain build-blocking gaps.

Reviewed argument recheck, trust approval, before/after tool hooks, permission ask, session, and message hooks. Argument mutation is guarded, but permission auto-allow and modified-payload provenance lack comparable controls.

Reviewed compaction, environment, prompt, return, registration, collision, and registry units. Central tool routing is safe by default; compaction conversion, privileged mutation, and universal fail-open semantics are unresolved.

Reviewed core-surface, host-policy, routing, config boundary/shape, disable persistence, and child compatibility units. Host boundaries are explicit; config-key identity and child dropped-capability visibility are underspecified.

Reviewed Persona silencing, event envelope/taxonomy, settings placement, inventory, add/remove, and config controls. Logging and inventory are concrete; destructive transactions, effective config state, privacy, and accessibility need closure.
